evidence: THE DECIDING LINE, read at source rather than inferred -- .tools/prd_signoff_lib.py, function `evaluate`: `current = (str(doc.get("half_hash") or "") == hashes[half]) if doc.get("half_hash") else (str(doc.get("prd_version")) == version)`. The else-branch is a LEGACY fallback to prd_version. The function's own docstring states it: 'CURRENT = half_hash equals the PRD's (or, legacy, prd_version equals).'

THE LIVE INSTANCE: org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/prd/signoff/4.0.0_SA_CRO.json reads {prd_pin: bbbf35c38e5e, prd_version: v0.4, signed_by: 4.0.0_SA_CRO~Z, verdict: SIGNED} -- NO `half` key and NO `half_hash` key. The PRD is still v0.4, so the legacy branch evaluates current=True.

rows.one_line: AC3's OWN INVOCATION DESTROYS UNCOMMITTED WORK IN THE FILE IT MUTATES. Its final limb is `git checkout -- src/pages/SecurityAnalysis/types.ts`, which restores that path from the INDEX, not from a pre-mutation snapshot -- so it reverts EVERY uncommitted edit in the file, not only the appended mutant. Run mid-work, as the criterion's own ordering invites, it silently deletes the cell's recut of the very file the mutant targets.

evidence: MEASURED IN THIS WORKTREE, 2026-09-12 ~00:0xZ: AC3 was run as written after `types.ts` had been recut (the MovementControl/SubjectControl/CrossedAxis/AxisResolution block and the RankTimePoint/TickerRankSeries/RankTimeSeriesSet block). It printed the expected `1` TS2322 hit, and the trailing `git checkout --` then restored the file to its committed state at `e6057f26`, discarding roughly 90 lines of this cell's own work. The loss was caught only because the harness echoed the restored file's contents back; nothing in the criterion's output says a revert happened.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT SPECIFIC TO THIS FILE OR THIS CELL: `git checkout -- <path>` is defined as 'overwrite the working-tree copy from the index'. Any criterion that mutates a TRACKED file in place and undoes the mutation with `git checkout --` has the same blast radius, and it is invisible in the criterion's own printed output because the count it reports is computed BEFORE the restore.

CLAUDE.md already carries the general form of this hazard under the worker bar ('never ... `checkout --` or `clean`'), which this criterion's text instructs the worker to do. The conflict is in the criterion, not in the worker's reading of it.

THE SAFE ORDERING EXISTS AND WAS USED HERE: run AC3 AFTER the commit that lands the cell's edits. Then the index carries the recut, `git checkout --` restores exactly that, and the criterion's restore-clause ('a criterion that leaves the mutant in the tree is NOT met') is satisfied with no collateral loss. Evidence of the safe ordering is this cell's own proof-of-spec, whose AC3 row records a post-commit run.

rows.spec_asserts: AC3's invocation reads `... >> src/pages/SecurityAnalysis/types.ts && <tsc> | grep -c TS2322; git checkout -- src/pages/SecurityAnalysis/types.ts`, and its expectation says 'The final `git checkout --` MUST restore the file' -- i.e. the restore is described as undoing the injected mutant.
rows.world_is: The restore is not scoped to the mutant. It is scoped to the FILE, and its source is the index, so it reverts the file to whatever was last committed or staged. On a cell that edits `types.ts` -- which this cell necessarily does, since the crossed-control types live there -- the criterion deletes the cell's work as a side effect of measuring the instrument.

evidence: THE CLONE HAS NO DEPENDENCIES, which is expected (`node_modules` is gitignored and a clone does not carry it) but is exactly what the two criteria need: `test -d node_modules` -> absent (printed `NO node_modules in clone`), against `258` entries in the main tree's `portal/node_modules`.

THE MANIFEST GRAIN WAS PROVEN BEFORE THE INSTALL WAS REUSED, blob by blob rather than by assumption: `package.json` `c17dea2964` at BOTH `c6728146` and `30ca034bba` (IDENTICAL); `bun.lock` `e88a7e989c` at both (IDENTICAL); `bun.lockb` and `package-lock.json` absent at both. NOTE THE NEGATIVE RESULT IN THE SAME SWEEP: `tsconfig.json` DIFFERS between them (`50da56ecfc` vs `1ffef600d9`), so the two trees are NOT interchangeable in general -- only the dependency manifest is.

TYPESCRIPT RESOLVES LOCALLY AND ITS VERSION IS RECORDED: `node_modules/typescript/package.json` -> `5.9.3`; `node_modules/.bin/tsc` present. `node --version` -> `v26.8.1`, `npx --version` -> `11.19.0`.

THE SHARED TREE WAS NOT WRITTEN THROUGH THE LINK: the first attempt junctioned `node_modules` WHOLE, which would have sent `tsconfig.app.json`'s `"tsBuildInfoFile": "./node_modules/.tmp/tsconfig.app.tsbuildinfo"` into the shared tree. Replaced with 262 per-package junctions plus a LOCAL real `.tmp` (`os.lstat(.tmp).st_reparse_tag == 0`). The shared tree's own `.tmp` still holds its two pre-existing `tsbuildinfo` files, and its entry count is unchanged at `263` before and after.

`os.path.islink` IS FALSE FOR AN NTFS JUNCTION IN THIS PYTHON (3.11), which is why the first removal attempt silently did nothing and reported `junctioned_dirs=0` while `entries_now=263`; the discriminating read is `os.lstat(p).st_reparse_tag == stat.IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT` -> `0xa0000003`. Removal used `os.rmdir` (which unlinks a junction and refuses a non-empty real directory), never `rmtree`, and the source was counted intact afterwards.

WHAT MAKES THIS RECORDABLE RATHER THAN MERELY INCONVENIENT: `2069` (AC2) and `1` (AC3) are only meaningful if the compiler that produced them is the one this commit's manifest pins, and nothing in either invocation prints the typescript version or the resolution source, so a re-run elsewhere could differ with no visible tell.

An always-fails criterion is not merely useless; it manufactures false evidence of the defect it was written to detect.
rows.notes: THE TEST APPLIED BEFORE AMENDING, stated because amending a criterion mid-round is exactly the shape in which an issuing seat could launder a failure: AN AMENDMENT THAT LETS A CRITERION DISCRIMINATE IS A REPAIR; ONE THAT LOWERS A BAR IS LAUNDERING. rows.spec_asserts: AMGT_RESAPP-Z-S38, written by this seat one tick earlier, states the remedy as: "RUN EVERY MECHANICAL CRITERION ONCE, AT THE CUT, AGAINST THE WORLD AS IT IS, AND CHECK THAT ITS OUTPUT COULD DIFFER IF THE CLAIM WERE FALSE."
rows.world_is: THAT RULE SILENTLY ASSUMES EVERY CRITERION GRADES THE CELL'S OWN REPAIR, AND SOME GRADE A GUARD INSTEAD. AC2 grades the repair, so the broken world IS the false-claim world and one run settles it. AC3 grades a REGRESSION GUARD -- 'the matcher was not loosened into matching everything' -- and that claim is TRUE in the broken world too, so running it there proves only that it is non-vacuous, never that it can fail. STAR: THE CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULE, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS RATHER THAN A LINE IN A LOG: BEFORE EXERCISING A CRITERION, NAME THE CLAIM IT GRADES -- THE CELL'S REPAIR, OR A GUARD AGAINST A DIFFERENT FAILURE. For a repair criterion the broken world is the control and it is free. For a guard criterion the false world must be MANUFACTURED, which is a mutation, which belongs to the worker under the mutation-control rule and never to a seat in a shared tree. WARN: A GUARD CRITERION THAT PASSES IN BOTH WORLDS IS NOT THEREBY VACUOUS -- and reading it as vacuous is the error this row is written to prevent in the next seat that runs the same check.
rows.notes: WHAT THIS ROW SETTLES FOR L9, addressed to 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z: the amended AC2 has a TWO-POINT CONTROL on the record -- 0 in the broken world, 183 in the repaired one, HEADER 13 in both -- taken by the ISSUING seat in a tree the worker does not control, so it is not the worker's self-report. The `At: <rel>:<line>` lines that AC1's grep counts carry the `rel` produced there.

THE TWO DISCOVERY CORPORA, CENSUSED BY SUBTRACTION OVER THEIR FULL DENOMINATORS: `infra/aws/lambda/ci/lambda-source-map.json` holds 214 entries, all 214 carrying a source path, of which **0** reach `lib/`, `research` or `scoped` (top roots: infra/aws=195, data/find=8, EXTERNAL/=8, tools/news_scanner=1, data/smartx=1, data/etfs=1). `infra/aws/ec2/EC2_MANIFEST.json` holds 27 services, 20 with an `iam_role`, of which **0** have a source_path reaching `lib/` or the repo root. THE ESTATE CONVENTION, FROM THIS PROJECT'S OWN SIBLING: `infra/aws/terraform/harvest/build-and-upload.sh:9` sets `SRC="$ROOT/infra/aws/lambda/research/pull_enqueue"`, and that package exists (`infra/aws/lambda/research/pull_enqueue/lambda_function.py`, 3978 bytes). The grant gives the module but not the source tree the module depends on.

AC1 MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER THE MOUNT LANDED, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, SO THE ZERO IS NOT A BROKEN READ: `timeout 110 comp-iam 2>&1 | grep -c -E "scoped_amgt|lib/research/api"` = **0** both before and after, against a POSITIVE CONTROL of **37** lines naming `infra/aws/lambda/` in the same 992-line output.

AND THE SHARPER MEASUREMENT, WHICH REFINES ROW Z-S27 RATHER THAN REPEATING IT: adding `infra/aws/terraform/harvest/scoped-amgt-api.tf` (a new IAM role, its policy, and eleven routes) DID move comp-iam's scanned-file denominator from **467 to 468 .tf files** -- so the tool demonstrably READ the new file -- while the RESOURCE PLANE line stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL (835 call(s) / 96 mapped role(s); 629 UNRESOLVABLE-RESOURCE / 142 GRANTED / 51 GRANTED-BROAD / 11 UNGRANTED / 2 GRANTED-ACTION-UNGRANTED-RESOURCE) and the new role name `opal-amgt-scoped-api` appears **0** times in the output.

rows.spec_asserts: AMGT-rf-2's AC1 `<expect>`, VERBATIM: "a printed integer STRICTLY GREATER THAN ZERO -- the adapter's call sites now APPEAR in `comp-iam`'s own output, which is the exact thing row `Z-S27` says is missing. ZERO IS THE MEASURED DEFECT and is NOT met." The cell body states the obligation as "to make the adapter call sites and their role binding APPEAR IN THE INSTRUMENT'S DENOMINATOR", and names the handler package as a deliverable: "Deliver the mount: the API Gateway route, the Lambda declaration, the handler package, the trusted edge boundary and the IAM." The order's `<paths>` grants `lib/research/api/*`, `infra/aws/terraform/amgt-resapp/`, `infra/aws/terraform/harvest/`, the channel, the two change-management paths and its own file -- nine entries. The same order instructs: "A SURFACE NOT NAMED IN `<paths>` IS A WALL ... Do not route around a missing path; file a row and stop on that clause."
rows.world_is: THE ORDER NAMES A DELIVERABLE AND A CRITERION THAT BOTH LIVE OUTSIDE ITS OWN GRANT, AND THE TWO HALVES ARE THE SAME OMISSION. `infra/aws/lambda/` is where every handler package in the estate lives, and `infra/aws/lambda/ci/lambda-source-map.json` is the ONLY thing that makes a package's calls visible to comp-iam. Neither is granted. So: (a) the HANDLER PACKAGE cannot be written at the location its own sibling uses; (b) AC1 cannot reach a non-zero integer by any act available inside the grant. WHAT WAS DELIVERED INSTEAD, because it IS in grant: the full terraform mount at `infra/aws/terraform/harvest/scoped-amgt-api.tf` -- the IAM role and a policy scoped to exactly the five DynamoDB call shapes the adapter makes (Query/GetItem/BatchGetItem on the table AND its index, PutItem/DeleteItem for star markers, no Scan anywhere), the Lambda declaration on the estate's yang-lambda module, the AWS_PROXY integration, all eleven routes, and the CUSTOM authorizer binding that makes the edge-injected X-Firm-Id trustworthy. WHAT IS OWED AND CANNOT BE PAID FROM HERE, listed in the .tf's own header so the next actor does not have to rediscover it: the package entrypoint under `infra/aws/lambda/research/scoped_amgt_api/`, the artifact build+upload with content-sha256 metadata, and the source-map entry. THE CONSEQUENCE THAT IS NOT OBVIOUS: A MOVED DENOMINATOR IS NOT EVIDENCE THE THING WAS VERDICTED. Row Z-S27's lesson was "an unchanged denominator after adding a consumer is proof the instrument never saw the consumer"; this run shows the WEAKER converse fails too -- the .tf count moved 467->468, proving comp-iam read the file, while zero verdicts changed and the new role never appears. A reader checking only 'did the denominator move?' would have recorded this as progress. The role is visible to the POLICY scan and invisible to the CALL scan, and those are two different corpora that a single summary line does not distinguish.
rows.notes: WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the mount is wrong or incomplete as terraform (it declares route, integration, Lambda, permission, role and policy, and the route set is drift-guarded against the adapter's own route table in both directions by `lib/research/api/tests/test_scoped_amgt_mount.py`). It does not claim comp-iam is defective -- verdicting calls against roles is what it is for, and it discloses its three scanned trees on its own summary line. It does not claim the IAM policy is WRONG; nothing here exercised it, which is precisely the gap. It does not assert WHY the grant omits these paths. NOTHING WAS DEPLOYED: no terraform apply, no artifact built or uploaded, nothing pushed -- so no NEVER-2 ledger entry was opened, because the obligation attaches to an act that can deploy and no such act was taken. rows.world_is: THE CRITERION'S INTENT IS SATISFIED AND ITS LITERAL BAND CLAUSE CANNOT BE, BY CONSTRUCTION, FOR ANY ARTIFACT BUILT THE WAY SECTION 1 ORDERS. So the precedent was followed and the discrepancy is recorded rather than designed around. A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING FOLDED IN BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME MEASUREMENT: this file's first draft built the route keys as "GET ${local.scoped_amgt_prefix}/...", and the census then returned ONE hit -- the prefix definition -- while the eleven mounted routes were invisible to every text instrument. rows.notes: WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim AC2 is unmet in substance -- the mount is declared in infrastructure and the census proves it with a printed denominator. It does not propose the JSON-contract pattern; that alternative is recorded only to show the band clause is satisfiable in principle and only by disobeying section 1. THE REUSABLE FORM: A CRITERION THAT NAMES AN INSTRUMENT'S CLASSIFICATION LABEL -- a band, a status token, an enum the tool emits -- MUST BE CHECKED AGAINST WHAT THAT INSTRUMENT ACTUALLY EMITS FOR THE ARTIFACT TYPE THE SAME ORDER MANDATES, and the cheap test is to run the census against an EXISTING correct artifact of that type before the cell starts. Here one command against a route that has been live for weeks would have shown SURFACED and caught the clause at cut time.

The cell's defect was a scope-name mismatch (`fiscal_year` vs `fiscal_year_line_item`); that is repaired and measurable. THE MATCHER SHORT-CIRCUITS ON None BEFORE IT EVER COMPARES A SCOPE: `_figures` opens `if not model_block: return []`. So the scope argument is never used and the result is [] for every possible input.
AC3 RUN VERBATIM RETURNS ITS EXPECTED VALUE ANYWAY: `WRONG_SCOPE=0`, rc 0. It passes, and it would pass identically against a matcher that returned all 196 figures for any scope.

Both numbers from the same object in the same call, so the zero is a true refusal and not an empty input.

THE ORDER ANTICIPATES THIS EXACT SHAPE IN ITS OWN SECTION 2: 'four projects' worth of cells converged in one evening on ONE defect class -- a criterion that cannot fail in the broken world ... you should treat a criterion that cannot fail as a defect worth a row even if it passes you.'

rows.spec_asserts: AMGT-rf-3's AC3 `<expect>`, VERBATIM: "`WRONG_SCOPE=0` -- the NEGATIVE CONTROL the slug asks for by name. A scope that does not exist must match NOTHING. If this returns a non-zero count the matcher has been loosened into matching everything, which would make AC2 pass for the wrong reason, and it is NOT met". rows.world_is: THE CONTROL IS WIRED TO None AND THEREFORE MEASURES NOTHING. Its stated job -- catching a matcher loosened into matching everything -- is precisely the job it cannot do, because the branch that would expose a loosened matcher is never reached. ⭐ AND THE FAILURE IS INVISIBLE AT EVERY POINT A READER WOULD LOOK: the invocation is well-formed, it runs clean, it prints exactly the expected token, and rc is 0. The only way to see it is to ask what `b.get('model_block')` actually is, which nothing in the criterion invites. THE CELL'S SUBSTANCE IS UNAFFECTED: the real negative control is landed as test_an_undeclared_scope_matches_nothing in lib/research/api/tests/test_fiscal_scope_contract.py, which loads the real block and asserts BOTH that the bogus scope matches 0 AND that the historically-wrong string 'fiscal_year' still matches 0 -- the second arm mattering because the tempting bad repair is to make every question work rather than to ask the right one. A ONE-CHARACTER-CLASS FIX WOULD MAKE AC3 REAL: filter `s.read_model_block('BABA_US_Equity')` instead of `b.get('model_block')`. That is the issuer's edit, not mine -- amending a criterion I am being graded on is not a worker act, and the order forbids guessing at intent.
rows.notes: WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim AC3's recorded verdict should be FAIL. Run as written it produced its expected output, so it is recorded PASS-by-output with this row attached -- which is what the order prescribes for a criterion that cannot fail. It does not claim the matcher is loosened (it is not: measured 0 for a bogus scope and 183 for the real one against the same real block). It does not claim `read_thesis_bundle` SHOULD return a `model_block` key -- adding one to satisfy a criterion would be shaping the artifact to fit its test, and the bundle deliberately returns the derived figure lists rather than the raw block. DISARM CONDITION, FALSIFIABLE: this row disarms when AC3's invocation filters a model block that is actually loaded -- i.e. when the same invocation, run against a matcher deliberately loosened to match everything, PRINTS A NON-ZERO VALUE. That is the test of a negative control: it must be shown to fire, not merely to agree. THE REUSABLE FORM: A NEGATIVE CONTROL MUST BE EXERCISED AGAINST THE BROKEN WORLD BEFORE IT IS TRUSTED IN THE FIXED ONE, and the cheapest version is to check that its INPUT is non-empty -- a control fed an empty or None subject returns the right answer for the wrong reason and is indistinguishable from a working one.

THE EFFECT OF DEFECT 2 ON THE CRITERION'S OWN CLAUSE: with the correct key, 'rows with full provenance' is 10 OF 110 on the criterion's own row set, while the cell's actual requirement -- every fiscal PX_LAST row carries its provenance -- is met 10 of 10. THE WORK ITSELF IS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED, so this row is about the criterion and not the cell: over the 10 real fiscal PX_LAST rows, rows reading the raw 146.58 = 0, all 10 are tagged RESOLVED, FY2025 serves 132.23 against raw 146.58, and each carries corrected_overlay_status + observation_date + derivation_key with its ORIGINAL vintage preserved (2026-09-10T23:20:19Z, distinct from the 2025-03-31 observation date). 56 of 56 tests pass across lib/research/api/tests and lib/research/rules/tests.

rows.world_is: A CRITERION WHOSE EVERY CLAUSE IS NEGATIVE OR UNIVERSAL IS SATISFIED BY AN EMPTY RESULT SET, AND THIS ONE RETURNS AN EMPTY SET. `PX_LAST_ROWS=0` is not a failure signal here -- it is a GREEN. rows.notes: WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the wiring is unmet in substance -- the corrected overlay is applied through the SHARED contract (lib/research/provenance/render_print.py, the Print path's own consumer), with no second implementation in the adapter, and both the RESOLVED and UNRESOLVED arms are exercised and asserted. It does not propose that read_model_block normalise the key -- that is the identity contract belonging to AMGT-s-12, the same reasoning as row Z-W11-S4, and taking it here to turn my own criterion green would be the worst possible reason to widen. A re-run that fixes only the key does NOT disarm it -- that run fails correct work and would be read as the cell being broken. THE REUSABLE FORM: BEFORE TRUSTING A CRITERION WHOSE CLAUSES ARE ALL NEGATIVE OR UNIVERSAL, CHECK THAT ITS RESULT SET IS NON-EMPTY, AND CHECK THAT ITS SELECTOR SELECTS ON A FIELD RATHER THAN ON THE TEXT OF A SERIALISED ROW. Both are one-line checks at cut time; neither is visible in the criterion's output, because an empty set and a correct world print the same green.

rows.one_line: AMGT-rf-5's AC2 REQUIRES A `CODE` BAND FROM `comp-find`, AND `comp-find` HAS NO SUCH BAND. Its band vocabulary is HEAD|DEF|SURFACED|CONFIG|TEST|DOC|COLD, printed by its own --help; `CODE` belongs to a DIFFERENT tool, `comp-read --enumerate`, whose bands are DOCSTRING|COMMENT|DEF|CODE. The criterion's two-sided test is exactly right in substance and names a band the invoked instrument can never emit.

evidence: THE INVOKED TOOL'S OWN VOCABULARY, from its own --help: `comp-find --help` -> `--band B  show only band B (HEAD|DEF|SURFACED|CONFIG|TEST|DOC|COLD)`. There is no CODE band. First-party source is banded SURFACED -- the tool prints its own gloss beside it: `[SURFACED] -- plain content match in first-party source`.

THE OTHER TOOL'S VOCABULARY, which is where `CODE` lives: `comp-read <file> --enumerate <regex>` prints `BANDS (sum to N): DOCSTRING / COMMENT / DEF / CODE`, observed repeatedly this session -- e.g. over build_zip.py (`DOCSTRING=1 COMMENT=0 DEF=1 CODE=1`) and over scoped_amgt.py (`DOCSTRING=0 COMMENT=0 DEF=1 CODE=12`). So the criterion mixed two tools' band vocabularies: it invokes comp-find and grades on comp-read's bands.

AC2 AS ACTUALLY RUN: `timeout 110 comp-find "UnprocessedKeys" lib/research --limit 20` -> `DENOMINATOR: 9 hit(s) across 88 file(s) scanned in scope [corpus=all] | 49 EPHEMERAL-FLOOR, NOT searched`, `BANDS (true totals, not this page): SURFACED=5 TEST=4`. Neither band is CODE, and neither can be.

THE CRITERION'S SUBSTANTIVE TEST IS NONETHELESS SATISFIED, on both of its refusal clauses: 'Hits only in TEST means the fake was taught the shape and the handler still ignores it' -- there are 5 first-party-source hits including the handler's actual read at lib/research/api/scoped_amgt.py:467, `((response.get("UnprocessedKeys") or {}).get(METRICS_TABLE) or {}).get("Keys") or []`. 'Hits only in CODE means nothing exercises the branch' -- there are 4 TEST hits, including the fake that returns the shape at test_unprocessed_keys.py:79. And the denominator is 88 files, not 0, so it is not out-of-corpus.

SAME CLASS AS ROW Z-W11-S3, DIFFERENT MECHANISM, WHICH IS WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ROW: S3 is rf-2's AC2 requiring CONFIG-or-DEF from comp-find for a terraform file -- both bands EXIST but neither is ever assigned to a .tf (68 of 68 route_key hits band SURFACED). Here the named band does not exist in the invoked tool at all.

rows.spec_asserts: AMGT-rf-5's AC2 `<expect>`, VERBATIM: "a PRINTED DENOMINATOR, with hits in BOTH the CODE band (the handler acts on the field) and the TEST band (a fake returns it). Hits only in TEST means the fake was taught the shape and the handler still ignores it, and is NOT met. Hits only in CODE means nothing exercises the branch, and is NOT met either. A denominator of 0 files scanned is OUT-OF-CORPUS, not a zero, and is NOT met". The invocation is `timeout 110 comp-find "UnprocessedKeys" lib/research --limit 20`.
rows.world_is: THE CRITERION IS RIGHT ABOUT WHAT TO CHECK AND WRONG ABOUT WHAT THE INSTRUMENT PRINTS. Its two-sided construction is the best-designed clause in this order -- it refuses a TEST-only result (a fake taught the shape while the handler still ignores it) AND a source-only result (a branch nothing exercises), so neither half can be faked independently. That test is fully satisfied here: 5 first-party-source hits including the handler's live read, and 4 TEST hits including the fake that produces the shape. ⛔ BUT THE BAND IT NAMES CANNOT APPEAR. `comp-find` emits SURFACED for first-party source and has no CODE band at all; CODE is `comp-read --enumerate`'s band, a different tool with a different vocabulary (DOCSTRING/COMMENT/DEF/CODE). So a grader applying the clause LITERALLY records NOT MET against correct, two-sided evidence. ⚠ AND THE DANGEROUS READING IS THE OTHER ONE: a worker who wanted a literal CODE band could reach for comp-read instead of the named comp-find, get DOCSTRING/COMMENT/DEF/CODE, and report a green -- having silently swapped the instrument the order specified. That is the worse failure, because it produces a passing line that nobody can reproduce with the invocation the order names. ⭐ THE SUBSTANCE HERE IS ALSO WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE BAND QUESTION: of the 5 source-side hits, TWO are executable code (:385 builds the incomplete-read reason string, :467 is the read of the field itself) and three are a comment and docstrings. A band count alone would not have distinguished those, and the clause's real requirement -- 'the handler ACTS on the field' -- is evidenced by :467 and by the behavioural tests under AC1, not by the band label.
rows.notes: WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim AC2 is unmet in substance -- both sides are present, with a printed non-zero denominator, and the handler demonstrably acts on the field. It does not claim comp-find's banding is wrong; SURFACED accurately describes a content match in first-party source. It does not propose swapping the invocation to comp-read: the order names comp-find and changing the instrument to make a label appear is the failure mode described above, not a fix. It does not re-grade row Z-W11-S3, which is the same class from a different cause. IT DOES NOT GRADE ITSELF: whether AC2 reads PASS on its substantive two-sided test or FAIL on its literal band name is 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z's adjudication at L9, and the instance records the raw output and both readings so no re-measurement is needed. DISARM CONDITION, FALSIFIABLE: this row disarms when AC2's clause names a band the INVOKED tool actually emits -- SURFACED for the handler side, TEST for the exercise side -- or when the clause drops band names and states the requirement it actually means (a first-party-source hit that is executable and a test hit that produces the shape). A re-run of the unchanged clause does not disarm it; the output will be SURFACED=5 TEST=4 every time. THE REUSABLE FORM: A CRITERION THAT NAMES AN INSTRUMENT'S OUTPUT VOCABULARY MUST NAME THE VOCABULARY OF THE INSTRUMENT IT INVOKES. Two comp-tools in this estate both print a line beginning 'BANDS' and their band sets are disjoint in the relevant members; one `--help` read at cut time distinguishes them.

THE REPAIR, and the part worth carrying off this project: two WRONG fixes were written before the right one and BOTH were caught by running the patched tool against the WHOLE ESTATE beside HEAD's copy at the same instant, not by testing the case that motivated the fix. (1) A 'status is a single bare token' test skipped legitimate prose statuses -- SPRING-CLEAN closures read 'complete -- SPRING-CLEAN ... THE FIX THAT HELD, and its prediction stated BEFORE the run: every spurious token in this corpus is an INLINE CODE SPAN -- prose ABOUT the tag. Masking code spans before locating the element (and slicing the value out of the ORIGINAL text, so a legitimate backticked value survives) satisfies both shapes. PREDICTION: exactly one project moves and the project SET is unchanged. RESULT: project set identical (49 both sides); one project moved, AMGT_RESAPP 9 ACTIVE -> 3 ACTIVE; totals 130 -> 124, and 130 - 124 = 6, the six round-7 orders that were wrongly ACTIVE. Committed at 5661885, commit-gate clean, lane ANY under .tools/**.

REMEDY, prospective and cheap: before using a literal token as a control, census it over the corpus and require zero AT THAT MOMENT; and in any document intended for citation, describe the control rather than printing its token, or use a token that cannot survive a quote. rows.notes: THE TWO RULES, both cheap and both prospective. rows.one_line: MY DRAIN-READINESS DRY RUN PRINTED 'THE WORKER'S BRANCH DROPPED 126 ROWS' AND THE WORKER'S BRANCH HAD DROPPED NOTHING. `git -C /c/tmp/...` invoked from NATIVE Python is Windows git, which cannot resolve an MSYS path: it returned rc=128 and an EMPTY document. That empty then entered a SET DIFFERENCE, and `base - theirs` over an empty side yields EVERY BASE ROW -- a perfectly well-formed, maximally alarming finding manufactured entirely by the instrument. THE CHECK I RAN TO DE-RISK THE DRAIN WAS ITSELF BROKEN IN THE DIRECTION THAT MANUFACTURES A DISASTER. Re-run with the Windows spelling: 126 base + 3 mine + 5 the worker's = 134, ZERO collisions, ZERO base rows dropped by either side.

evidence: THE DEFECT REPRODUCED DELIBERATELY, one question and two path spellings, run side by side so the difference is the measurement and not a story: `git -C /c/tmp/wk-amgt-9-1 show wk-amgt_resapp-9-1:<channel>` returns rc=128, 0 bytes, stderr `fatal: cannot change to '/c/tmp/wk-amgt-9-1': No such file or directory`; `git -C C:/tmp/wk-amgt-9-1 ...` returns rc=0, 645890 bytes, stderr empty. The subprocess inherits NATIVE Windows git, which does not resolve the MSYS mount prefix that the Bash tool resolves fine.

HOW A ZERO BECAME A CATASTROPHE, and this is the part that generalises: the empty document produced an EMPTY ID SET, which was then fed to `base - theirs`. A set difference against an empty right-hand side returns the WHOLE left-hand side, so the run printed all 126 base row ids under the heading `base rows lost by theirs`. It is not malformed, it is not an exception, and it is the single most alarming reading the check can produce.

THE CORRECTED RUN, with rc ASSERTED on every read before any arithmetic and each input's non-emptiness as its own positive control: SITEZ HEAD 129 ids / 639289 bytes; worker branch tip 131 ids / 645890 bytes; common base 8af6dbbe88 126 ids / 620559 bytes. ONLY MINE since base: Z-S68, Z-S69, Z-S70. ONLY THEIRS: Z-W15-S1 through S5. Base rows dropped by mine NONE, by theirs NONE. Colliding new ids NONE. UNION 134 = 126 + 3 + 5.

SO THE DRAIN ITSELF IS CLEAN AND THAT IS THE ANSWER THE CHECK WAS ASKED FOR: the two sides append disjoint id namespaces -- the seat mints `Z-S<k>` and the worker mints `Z-W15-S<k>` -- so the union is a pure concatenation with no renumbering owed. That separation is exactly why the channel header specifies both grammars.

AND THE READINESS HALF PASSED TOO: the union-merge helper is present at 3930 bytes, and `.tools/safe-merge.sh` at HEAD is 21704 bytes with 24 occurrences of `--continue`, so the conflicted-drain limb the drain depends on is still in the file rather than remembered.

rows.spec_asserts: Rule 22 and the estate's banked instrument law both say an empty result is a value, not an absence, and that a read whose emptiness carries a verdict must never be run without a control. The device already banks two instances of this exact class -- native Python cannot read a /cygdrive path, and an aws shim crash reads as an EMPTY result.
rows.world_is: I knew both and still shipped a third instance, in the one check whose whole purpose was to de-risk an act. STAR: AN EMPTY READ ENTERING A SET DIFFERENCE MANUFACTURES ITS OWN MAXIMAL FINDING. The other two banked instances fail toward a benign-looking ZERO -- nothing found, all clear -- which is dangerous because it gets acted on quietly. THIS ONE INVERTS: the empty side is the SUBTRAHEND, so the arithmetic converts silence into the loudest possible alarm, and the alarm is well-formed, itemised and specific. WARN: a false ALL-CLEAR gets believed; a false CATASTROPHE gets ACTED ON, and the act here would have been to halt a drain, re-cut a worker's branch, or open an incident about 126 rows that were never at risk.
rows.notes: THE GUARD, and it is arithmetic-shaped rather than path-shaped, because fixing only the path would be the remedy-scoped-to-where-you-got-caught error one field over: (1) ASSERT rc==0 AND non-empty ON EVERY READ BEFORE ANY SET OPERATION CONSUMES IT -- a comparison is not allowed to run on an input nobody confirmed; (2) PRINT EACH INPUT'S SIZE BESIDE THE VERDICT so an empty side is visible in the same output as the conclusion it produced; (3) when a difference returns something close to the WHOLE of one side, treat that as an INSTRUMENT reading first and a world reading second -- a peer does not usually delete a hundred rows. AND THE PATH RULE THIS SITS ON: inside the Bash tool `/c/...` resolves, but any subprocess that reaches NATIVE Windows git or python needs `C:/...`; the two spellings name the same directory and only one of them answers. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT DO: it does not claim the drain is at risk -- the corrected run says the union is clean at 134 with zero collisions -- and it does not touch the worker's branch, which is mid-pass. DISARM CONDITION, falsifiable: the round-9 drain runs its union check with rc and non-emptiness asserted on every input and the three sizes printed beside the verdict, and lands 134 distinct ids with no renumbering.

rows.one_line: AC3's invocation curls 127.0.0.1:5175 but vite binds [::1]:5175 ONLY on this device, so the criterion as written reads HTTP 000 for a perfectly healthy server -- it cannot tell a working dev server from a dead one, and its failure arm is the ONLY arm it can reach.

evidence: THE INVOCATION AS WRITTEN, run verbatim from org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/task-orders/AMGT_RESAPP.TO-AMGT-rh-1.the-served-route-end-to-end.md@e2ff1ae12f: 'curl: (7) Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1:5175 after 2013 ms: Could not connect to server' / 'HTTP 000 bytes 0' / 'NEG 000'. Both arms 000.

THE SERVER WAS HEALTHY AT THAT MOMENT, from the same run's own log tail: 'VITE v7.3.5 ready in 427 ms' and 'Local: http://localhost:5175/'. The criterion's own sub-requirement -- 'the vite log's first lines must show the server bound to the port' -- was SATISFIED in the same breath as its main probe returned 000.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, netstat -ano at that moment: 'TCP [::1]:5175 [::]:0 LISTENING 9184' and NO 127.0.0.1:5175 listener of any kind. vite's default host is 'localhost', which this Node resolves to the IPv6 loopback first and binds there exclusively.

REPRODUCED ON A SECOND, INDEPENDENT SERVER START (pid 26404): 'TCP [::1]:5175 [::]:0 LISTENING 26404'. Not a flake, and not a strictPort collision -- the port bound is 5175 exactly, so the order's 'something else holds 5175' reading is FALSIFIED rather than merely untested.
THE SAME SERVER ANSWERS ON THE ADDRESS IT ACTUALLY BOUND: 'ROOT(localhost) HTTP 200 bytes 826'. One address reads 000 and the other 200, same server, same second.
PRE-STATE CONTROL, run BEFORE any server start: 'PRE 000' with 'Could not connect' and no listener on 5175 -- so the later 200 is caused by this worker's server and not by a pre-existing one.

rows.spec_asserts: AC3 asserts that curling http://127.0.0.1:5175/ against a locally started vite dev server yields 'HTTP 200 with a non-zero byte count on the root', and treats a failure to connect as evidence about the server (its only named failure reading is a strictPort collision: 'something else holds 5175 and that is a row, not a retry on another port').
rows.world_is: vite binds the IPv6 loopback [::1]:5175 ONLY, so 127.0.0.1:5175 refuses the connection no matter how healthy the server is. THE CRITERION IS THE 'ALWAYS-FAILS' SHAPE: its output is HTTP 000 for a healthy server, for a dead one, and for a crashed one alike, so nothing it prints carries information. STAR: THE FAILURE IS NOT THE SERVER AND IT IS NOT THE PORT -- IT IS THE ADDRESS, and the order's only offered reading of a non-200 (a strictPort collision) points at the one cause that was measurably absent. A worker following the order literally would have filed 'the dev server does not serve' about a server that was serving.
rows.notes: REMEDY, cheap and prospective: curl http://localhost:5175/ rather than the literal 127.0.0.1, or start vite with --host 127.0.0.1 so the bind matches the probe. GENERAL SHAPE, which is why this is a row rather than a footnote: A HARDCODED LOOPBACK LITERAL IS A BIND-ADDRESS ASSUMPTION WEARING THE COSTUME OF A NEUTRAL PROBE. 'localhost' and '127.0.0.1' are the same host to a human and different sockets to Node on this device. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM: that the route does not serve -- it does, measured separately and recorded in the instance; and that AC3 would pass if the address were fixed -- it would not, for the SEPARATE and more interesting reason filed at AMGT_RESAPP-Z-W15-S2. DISARM: not required; nothing is armed. The defect is confined to one criterion's text in one order and the served-route fact is established by other evidence in the same instance.

The consequence is that AC3's negative control is the 'always-passes' shape and is unsatisfiable BY CONSTRUCTION for this class of application: there is no path, nonsense or real, for which this control could ever return anything but 200. rows.notes: REMEDY, and it needs no new instrument because the order's own worktree already contains one: grade the route through the MODULE GRAPH, where a real module returns transformed source and an absent one returns the 826-byte fallback (a >15x byte separation with a firing negative control), or drive a browser -- which this cell explicitly and correctly excludes from worker scope. rows.world_is: THAT FORM IS UNCOMMITTABLE ON THIS FABRIC AND THE GATE SAYS SO IN ONE LINE. ID_RE at .tools/surprise-row-gate.py:104 really does make (Z-)? optional, and org/surprise_channel/schemas/investigation_item.schema.json really does carry the same optional group -- so two independent surfaces agreed with each other and BOTH WERE BLIND to a third limb that couples the infix to the fabric enum. Piped through cat -A so the terminator is visible: the aliased 'ls -1' renders the directory entry as read/$ while 'command ls -1' (alias bypassed) renders it as read$ and 'ls -1 --indicator-style=none' renders read$. So the trailing slash is the -F classifier, present only on the aliased form -- which is the form the tick expression used.

THE DEFECT IS THE ANCHOR. The tick counts with: ls -1 <inbox> | grep -v '^read$' | grep -cv '^$'. Against read/ the pattern ^read$ cannot match, so the directory survives the filter and is counted as an undrained message. The filter is not merely weak here, it is INOPERATIVE -- it removes nothing at all.

THE DISCREPANCY, at one instant: the expression returned 4 while 'ls -1 <inbox>/*.md | wc -l' returned 3. The three are the real population and each was read by name: 20260913T061447Z from 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z (msg 22301, the rh-1 AC6 framing), 20260913T062709Z from this seat (the AMGT_RESAPP round-9 L8 packet), and 20260913T075455Z from 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z (msg 22327, the POSN_ASTTAX round-4 L8 packet). rows.one_line: ALL SEVEN GRADUATE AS ONE CLASS, AND IT IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE CLASS IN THIS CHANNEL: A CRITERION WHOSE INVOCATION CANNOT BE SATISFIED BY A CORRECT BUILD IS NOT A WEAK CRITERION, IT IS A NON-CRITERION -- it returns the same verdict on a correct world and a broken one, so nothing about the estate can move it. Three are ALWAYS-FAILS by construction: W7-S1 (AC4's string check cannot match the TO-NAMED tool's own hardcoded Status value), W2-S2 (AC6 greps `comp-routes behaviors`, which prints STATIC hand-authored comments and structurally cannot show a pure-add route; the route IS visible under the `api-routes` subcommand AC6 does not name), W3-S4 (AMGT-s-9's AC2 reads a top-level `figure_ids` key that NONE of AMGT-s-1's three landed files carries, because figures are keyed by a (scope, fiscal_year, mnemonic) tuple there). One is JOINTLY UNSATISFIABLE: W7-S5, where the issuer's instruction and the owned-paths gate cannot both be obeyed, because a TERMINAL order is not a live grant. Two are FACE-VS-GATE disagreements on the same field: W3-S2 and W7-S2, the proof-of-spec filename, where the worker face names a shorter stem than the gate's discovery glob requires. One is an INSTRUMENT GRAIN defect: S2, where receiving-check.py grades one file at a time so an issuance-set coverage limb refuses every member (owns 1 of 16) while the same gate over the set passes 16 of 16.

evidence: THE COMMON PROPERTY, and it is what makes these one row rather than seven: in every case the criterion's verdict is INDEPENDENT of the thing it purports to measure. A correct build and a broken one produce the identical output, so the criterion carries zero discriminating power and its PASS or FAIL says nothing. That is the always-fails member of the three shapes (always-fails / always-passes / unsatisfiable-honest).

W2-S2 IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE BECAUSE THE EVIDENCE THE CRITERION WANTED DOES EXIST, one subcommand away: `comp-routes behaviors` renders each behavior's static hand-authored comment, never a computed route list, so no amount of correct building makes a new route appear there; `comp-routes api-routes` shows the declared route. The criterion named the wrong instrument, not a missing capability -- which is the version of this defect that wastes the most time, because the build is right and the reading is wrong.

A criterion must be run against the world BEFORE it is handed to a worker, and against the TOOL THE ORDER NAMES rather than against an imagined equivalent.

rows.one_line: DISMISSED -- the only row in this channel whose defect was fully inside its own author's grant and is already fixed with nothing residual. There is no remedy owed to anyone and no hazard that outlives the round, so graduating it would mint a remediation item nothing would act on.

evidence: The row's own text places the defect, the fix and the write surface in one place: build_view.py is the worker's own file, inside its own <paths>, and the correction was made in-session. No other cell's artifact and no served surface is implicated.

THE REASON IT WAS INVISIBLE IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, and it is why the dismissal is of the ROW and not of the lesson: an empty store returns no matches, and a key that matches NOTHING also returns no matches. The two states are indistinguishable until real data lands. So the defect was undetectable for as long as its detector had nothing to detect against -- a criterion exercised against an empty store cannot discriminate a correct key from a broken one.

DISMISSED IS THE CORRECT DISPOSITION RATHER THAN GRADUATED, on this channel's own convention: GRADUATED carries a finding forward to an owner, and there is no owner and no forward act here. The fix is landed, the paths are the author's, and the hazard cannot recur on this artifact.

rows.one_line: GRADUATES, AND IT IS THE ONE ROW WHOSE DISPOSITION IS NOT THE END OF ITS STORY: W9-S2 is the external TLS block on AMGT-s-b4. astn/brightdata/residential-proxy TLS-intercepts every HTTPS GET with an untrusted 'Bright Data Proxy Root CA' leaf no standard client can verify, so all 9 attempted GETs across 3 tickers failed AT THE HANDSHAKE, before reaching Seeking Alpha, and AC1 honestly reads 0 of 3 landed. ⭐ THE GRADE THAT MATTERS HERE IS THE ONE THE ROW ARGUES FOR AND I CONFIRM: THIS IS NOT A DEFECT IN THE ORDER'S OWN WORK. The fetcher, the detectors and the logging are sound and AC2 through AC6 all pass; the deliverable is otherwise complete and the failure is an HONEST TLS FAIL at a layer outside the cell's write surface. An externally-blocked criterion that reports its own blockage accurately is behaving correctly -- it is the one shape of failure that should NOT be re-cut.

evidence: THE FAILURE LAYER IS NAMED AND IT IS BELOW THE CELL: the handshake fails on an untrusted re-signing root, so no request ever reaches Seeking Alpha. Nothing the fetcher could do differently changes that, and the row does not ask for a workaround -- notably it does NOT propose disabling verification, which would have converted an honest block into a silent trust defect.

THE CELL'S OWN WORK IS EVIDENCED SEPARATELY FROM THE BLOCK: AC2 through AC6 pass, which is what distinguishes 'the order failed' from 'the world refused'. A row that could not make that distinction would leave the cell's quality unknown.

THE GATE THIS ROW SITS ON IS NOT THIS SEAT'S, and 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z stated the two paths in msg 21143: either the proxy path is resolved and s-b4 re-runs to completion, or a ruling makes its externally-blocked state terminal for the round with FWD-4's Seeking-Alpha half graded NOT_REALIZED/blocked. grades.reason: BOTH LIMBS MET. LIMB 1 (could an analyst answer 'where from, on what basis, as of when' from the record alone): YES on a named ADR figure -- BABA US Equity FY2025 EBITDA_ADJUSTED 209364.0, unit MILLIONS, sign POSITIVE, basis {mnemonic, Bloomberg's-own-definition}, vintage, source bloomberg-dapi. LIMB 2 (is a differing unit carried as a PER-SECURITY fact rather than smoothed): YES -- field_map.json carries 0 unit-family divergences across the three securities, and the one real divergence found (a currency/basis difference on the ADR) is recorded in per_security_detail + cross_security_findings[0] AND propagated into every affected figure. ⭐ WHAT LIFTS THIS ABOVE A BARE PASS: the record DISCLOSES what it cannot resolve (which currency the MILLIONS figure is denominated in) through an explicit currency_caveat rather than shipping a bare number. A figure that names its own unresolved dimension is answerable; one that hides it is not, and the bar is about answerability.

PASS ON THE BAR AS WRITTEN, AND THE BAR'S OWN WORRY IS LIVE ON A ROUTE IT DOES NOT NAME -- both halves stated because the second is the useful one. THE NAMED SCENARIO IS HANDLED: bloomberg_health() runs BEFORE every pull and on ok:False writes packs/<key>/status.json {state: FAILED, reason: 'terminal signed out (bloomberg_health ok=False): <error>'} then deletes the SQS message -- so the analyst who submits while the terminal is signed out sees REQUESTED -> FAILED with a human-readable reason. A MARKED failure, which is exactly what the bar asks for, and 'honest about its latency' is met by SEAM_DESIGN s.6's measured 7.6s/7.7s stated as conditional on a consumer running. ⚠ BUT THE ASSIGNEE DISCLOSED A SECOND INPUT THE BAR DOES NOT ENUMERATE AND IT PRODUCES PRECISELY THE ANTI-PATTERN THE BAR FEARS: with NO consumer running at all (the poller is person-started, never a persistent service) a request sits at REQUESTED indefinitely, no FAILED/timeout is ever written, and status.json cannot distinguish 'about to be picked up' from 'no consumer will ever run' -- i.e. a page that looks like it is still fetching an hour later. I grade PASS because the criterion's subject is the SIGNED-OUT path and because 'honest about its failure modes' is satisfied by disclosure, not by having none. The gap GRADUATES as a finding rather than lowering this grade, and the assignee earned the pass by naming it instead of leaving it to be found in production.

MET, AND THE INTERESTING CASE IS THE ONE THAT MARKS ITSELF. IS_DIV_PER_SHR on the same mnemonic across three securities: SAP and BABA render fully self-sufficient lines ('<value> PER SHARE (local trading/reporting currency) ... IS_DIV_PER_SHR (Dividend per share.) ... as of <vintage> ... Bloomberg') -- an analyst answers basis and as-of without a spreadsheet. BA US Equity renders '[UNRESOLVED UNIT]' on all ten fiscal years, and THAT IS THE CORRECT BEHAVIOUR FOR THE BAR: the line still answers source and vintage, withholds only the per-share unit, and provenance_session_log.md names the root cause. A marked value, never a blank and never a guess. ⛔ THE ROOT CAUSE IS A REAL UPSTREAM DEFECT AND I AM NAMING IT RATHER THAN LETTING THE PASS ABSORB IT: AMGT-s-1's field map classified Boeing's unit from its MOST RECENT fiscal year, which is post-dividend-suspension and zero-valued, and the resulting status applies PER-SECURITY rather than per-fiscal-year -- so one unrepresentative sampled year marks ten years of real dividends unresolved. Sampling the latest period to classify a unit fails exactly on securities whose latest period is atypical. That belongs to AMGT-s-1's map, not to this cell, and this cell's rendering of it is right.

⛔ I CANNOT GRADE THIS AGAINST ITS OWN BAR, AND SAYING SO IS THE HONEST OUTPUT RATHER THAN CONVERTING AN ABSENT INPUT INTO A VERDICT. The bar opens 'for one security THAT HAD SA RAW LANDED'. At the graded vintage ZERO securities had: run_summary.json records sa_raw_keys_found 0, because AMGT-s-b4 was proxy-blocked at the TLS layer (row AMGT_RESAPP-Z-W9-S2). So the bar's own precondition did not exist and the population it names was empty. WHAT THE ASSIGNEE DID INSTEAD IS SOUND AND IS NOT WHAT THIS CRITERION ASKS: it ranked the non-SA corpus and the ordering is defensible -- a Reuters item dated 2026-09-08 (PROVISIONAL, 3 mentions) ranks ABOVE a Bloomberg sector roundup dated 2026-09-01 (REFUSE, 10 mentions), so recency beats mention-count, matching 'most recent' first; both non-PASS reasons are specific and actionable without opening the source; the ir-class absence is not silent (identity_dropped names ir_domain and quotes render_together's refusal verbatim); and the SA half is stated absent-with-reason rather than invented. On a non-SA population I would grade that PASS. ⭐ AND THE OPERATIVE POINT FOR THE ROUND: SA RAW HAS NOW LANDED. AMGT-s-b4's re-run put 18 raw objects across 3 tickers in S3 at 2026-09-11T04:02Z, so this criterion IS NOW EXERCISABLE and was not when it was answered. It should be re-run against the landed SA data -- a round-2 item, not a defect in this cell. A criterion whose precondition arrives AFTER it is answered needs re-exercising, not re-writing.

MET ON BOTH LIMBS, AND THE FIRST LIMB'S DISJUNCTION IS ANSWERED BY REJECTING BOTH HORNS, WHICH IS THE RIGHT ANSWER. The bar asks: would Adam forward this unreformatted, OR does it read as a screenshot of a dashboard? The render is NEITHER -- it is a DOCUMENT (same section labels, same order, own page per block, no UI chrome) carrying the honest skeleton, with every analyst-authored block marked [MACHINE-EMPTY] where the real pack holds ~9,000 characters of prose, bio and custom analysis. NOT-YET-FORWARDABLE IS NOT A FAILURE HERE: the pack's substance is analyst-authored, so no renderer could supply it, and marking those blocks empty is the only honest option available -- inventing prose to make it forwardable is the failure this bar exists to prevent. ⭐ AND ONE MEASURED PLACE IT BEATS THE REAL PACK: page 1's model block carries MORE per-figure provenance (unit, mnemonic, Bloomberg definition, vintage, source) than the real pack's own bare financial-summary table. LIMB 2 (does the spec say, per surface, what shows when that surface is NOT there): YES, 15 of 15 DESIGN_SPEC sections name an UNRESOLVED/FAILED/HELD-BACK or stated-absence behaviour, cited per surface.

MET, AND ON THE STRONGER FORM OF EACH NAMED PROPERTY. The bar's test is whether STORE_CONTRACT.md lets AMGT-s-1 land raw bytes and AMGT-s-14 render last-run/outcome/re-run WITHOUT ASKING ANYONE. All four named rules are stated: raw-before-derived (s.1, and made STRUCTURAL rather than conventional -- a derived/packs writer reads an existing raw/ key as its input, so there is nothing to derive from until raw/ exists, which is a property no one can forget); a stamp per write (s.3, pinned to UTC-at-write-start rather than the vendor as_of, mirroring the OPAL_ASSETS run_date-vs-as_of lesson, with >=1 stamp per stage answering AMGT-s-14's own 'a single refresh under one timestamp is a violation' bar); never write to an existing path (s.4, with versioning named as the safety net and NOT the mechanism); and the latest stamp as the read (s.4, the lexicographically-greatest stamp, computable from list-objects-v2 --delimiter / CommonPrefixes with NO index or pointer file -- so the read needs no second artifact anyone could forget to update). s.2 pins security_key to AMGT-s-12's identity layer, identical across all three prefixes, and states explicitly that a vendor's own id (sa_id, CIK, CUSIP) is never the key. ⭐ s.5 answers AMGT-s-14's four questions CONCRETELY -- source, last run, outcome, re-run-alone -- which is the actual 'without asking anyone' test, and the assignee notes it went past the order's literal item (b) to do it.

MET ON BOTH LIMBS, with one readability consequence recorded. LIMB 1 (would Adam find the stalest name in one glance without opening a folder): the sort rule is explicit in SPEC_SECTION_freshness.md s.2 -- ascending by last_refreshed with NEVER sorted to the TOP -- so the first row a reader's eye reaches is always the stalest or the first NEVER. No scan, search or filter. The spec's choice to treat NEVER as stalest is coherent and defensible -- a never-researched name does need attention most -- but 'one glance' degrades as the NEVER block grows, and it will shrink only as coverage lands. Worth a look when the ordering is built. ⭐ And s.7 states the single generated_at caption as the ONLY page-level freshness signal, explicitly not implying anything runs on its own, which is the correct posture under this estate's monitor moratorium.

MET, AND LIMB 2 IS PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSERTED, which is unusual and worth the pass on its own. LIMB 1 (is the reason one an analyst would accept rather than a blank): YES -- the absent record carries basis 'absent', members [], a vintage, and a reason that names WHY ('candidate universe not classified; a quota decision (F2) precedes derivation'), plus the fact that the subject's OWN GICS_SECTOR_NAME is known ('Consumer Discretionary') while no other covered name has been classified by that field, so no candidate can be tested. MET ON BOTH LIMBS, and limb 2 carries a real negative control. LIMB 1 (is the drafted sentence unmistakably a machine's starting point rather than the firm's view): YES. The shipped sentence is 'Recent coverage notes that "revenue growth as AI demand accelerates" (Reuters).' The lead-in hedges the claim to the source, and the assignee states the contrast that makes it testable rather than stylistic -- a firm view would read 'Alibaba's cloud revenue accelerated', asserting in the firm's own voice. The quoted span is verbatim from the Reuters item's own title, with the evidence id carried beside it. LIMB 2 (is the verbatim normalisation tight enough that a near-quote could not slip through as verbatim): YES, and this is the strong part. The normalisation is CLOSED and enumerated -- exactly three transformations (curly-quote straightening, casefold, whitespace collapse) 'and nothing else' -- so its admit set is bounded by construction. Both arms are exercised: a case/whitespace variant and a curly-quote source both ADMIT, a genuine paraphrase REFUSES, and a mutant control backs it. ⭐ THE ARGUMENT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT EMPIRICAL: a paraphrase uses different words, and none of the three named transformations can turn different words into a substring match -- so refusal follows from the closure of the transformation set, not from having tested enough paraphrases.

⛔ FAILS ON LIMB 2, AND THE ASSIGNEE'S OWN EVIDENCE IS WHAT FAILS IT. I am not softening this because the disclosure was exemplary -- honesty earns an accurate grade, not a pass. LIMB 1 PASSES DECISIVELY: a REFUSE renders as bracketed text WHERE A NUMBER WOULD BE ('[REFUSED: EBITDA_FIXTURE: unit/sign convention is 'INFERRED', not MEASURED]'), so a scanning analyst sees a broken-looking cell and a REFUSE cannot be mistaken for a value at all. That is the bar's failure condition in the bar's own words. THE CAUSE IS NAMED AND THE REMEDY IS ALREADY SCOPED: bracket text alone is not equally salient to a REFUSE bracket, and SPEC_SECTION_checkface.md says the eventual .tsx needs a DIFFERENT visual marker (colour or icon) for PROVISIONAL -- a deferred design decision this cell's plaintext render could not supply. ⚠ WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A COSMETIC NIT: PROVISIONAL exists to stop an unchecked figure being read as checked. A marker that is skimmed as 'fine' does not do that, so the held-back rule is present in the data and absent in the reading -- the number ships looking checked. This grade is a GATE on the check-face surface: the visual marker lands before the .tsx serves PROVISIONAL figures to an analyst.

MET ON BOTH LIMBS, with the assignee's own calibration accepted. LIMB 1 (are the six refusal inputs REAL rather than strawmen): YES in substance -- figure traces to 8 Bloomberg mnemonics tested against FactSet's 2.65 with none reproducing it; peer to ASML NA's own CSC sheet MEASURED carrying the full 12-ticker KPN telecom set verbatim; identity to the T CN (Telus) / T US (AT&T) collision with BOTH tickers present in the same corpus's own KPN peer set, a real same-symbol/different-company case; sentence to a paraphrase of the field map's own s.5 sentence, differing only in wording, which is precisely the shape C-VERBATIM-GATE exists to catch. ⭐ AND IT DECLARES ITS WEAKEST LINK RATHER THAN LETTING ME FIND IT: item's headline and source's aggregator domain are CONSTRUCTED shapes over a MEASURED pattern, not measured instances, because this cell has no word to fetch content (G-24). MET ON BOTH LIMBS, and limb 2 is the best-controlled reproducibility claim in this round. LIMB 1 (does the deliverable say, plainly and PER KEY, what it could not resolve and why): YES, key by key -- bloomberg_ticker is MEASURED-or-UNRESOLVED with workbook path plus sheet/cell evidence and NEVER from the folder name; sa_symbol is INFERRED only for US names via a stated ticker-root rule with the rule and input named, UNRESOLVED everywhere else and never MEASURED; ir_domain and social_account are UNRESOLVED everywhere with evidence naming the missing vendor word (G-24). ⭐ AND AMENDMENT 1 IS THE HONEST HANDLING OF THE DEFECT I VERIFIED SEPARATELY AT C-S1: a MEASURED candidate that turns out to be a template placeholder shared by 2+ folders is downgraded to UNRESOLVED **with the shared value recorded and the sibling folders named** -- so a reader can see what was removed and why, which is what makes the downgrade auditable instead of a silent number change. A determinism control with the timestamps masked is the right instrument: it separates genuine non-determinism from the clock, which a naive re-run conflates.

PASS ON THE OPERATIVE LIMB, and the bar's literal phrasing conflicts with its own order -- both stated. THE BAR ASKS whether the next worker could get all five observables in one call OR WOULD HAVE TO RE-PLAN. The answer to the operative clause is NO RE-PLANNING IS NEEDED: DATASET_IDS, FIRST_RUN_DATASET_ID, FIRST_RUN_COMPANY, QUERY_ATTEMPTS with its STOP_RULE, OBSERVABLES, COST_CAP_USD with cost_cap_exceeded(), CANNOT_SERVE_SIGNAL and FOURTH_SURFACE_NOTE are all module-level data that compose_request() already reads, and main() already accepts --word-record and clears the G-24 gate. ⛔ FAILS ON LIMB 1, on the assignee's own declared weakest link, and the failure is structural rather than a matter of degree. THE BAR ASKS whether the official-vs-impostor test 'would ACTUALLY separate a fan account from the company's own'. THE TEST IS AN **OR** OF THREE CHECKS: (1) the company's own measured web presence links the account by exact URL; (2) the platform's verification mark is present; (3) the account's bio names the company's registered domain. It does clear the TRIVIAL case -- a same-name parody with no cross-link, no mark and a bio naming nothing satisfies none of the three and is correctly excluded, which a bare name-match would not do. ⛔ BUT BECAUSE THE COMPOSITION IS A BARE OR, CHECK (3) ALONE ADMITS, AND CHECK (3) IS CHEAPLY GAMEABLE: an impostor copies the same 'official account of <domain>' bio text a real account carries and is ADMITTED on that basis, with no requirement that (3) co-occur with (1) or (2). The assignee states this outright and also that check (2) is weaker than it reads, a paid verification mark having been decoupled from identity verification on at least one major platform since 2023. So an impostor needs to beat only the WEAKEST of three checks, and two of the three are individually beatable. ⚠ THE OR IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE CHECKS: three weak-to-strong signals combined by OR are exactly as strong as the weakest one, which inverts the intent of listing three. THE DECIDING LINE, read at source rather than inferred -- .tools/prd_signoff_lib.py, function `evaluate`: `current = (str(doc.get("half_hash") or "") == hashes[half]) if doc.get("half_hash") else (str(doc.get("prd_version")) == version)`. The else-branch is a LEGACY fallback to prd_version. The function's own docstring states it: 'CURRENT = half_hash equals the PRD's (or, legacy, prd_version equals).'

THE LIVE INSTANCE: org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/prd/signoff/4.0.0_SA_CRO.json reads {prd_pin: bbbf35c38e5e, prd_version: v0.4, signed_by: 4.0.0_SA_CRO~Z, verdict: SIGNED} -- NO `half` key and NO `half_hash` key. The PRD is still v0.4, so the legacy branch evaluates current=True.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT SPECIFIC TO THIS FILE OR THIS CELL: `git checkout -- <path>` is defined as 'overwrite the working-tree copy from the index'. THE SAFE ORDERING EXISTS AND WAS USED HERE: run AC3 AFTER the commit that lands the cell's edits. Then the index carries the recut, `git checkout --` restores exactly that, and the criterion's restore-clause ('a criterion that leaves the mutant in the tree is NOT met') is satisfied with no collateral loss. Evidence of the safe ordering is this cell's own proof-of-spec, whose AC3 row records a post-commit run.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: is the chosen shape honest about its latency and its failure modes -- would an analyst who typed a ticker while the terminal was signed out see a MARKED failure with a reason, or a page that looks like it is still fetching an hour later?
acceptance.invocation: org/missions/D5/AMGT/AMGT_RESAPP/deliverables/0.9.0_WK_AMGT_RESAPP~2/SEAM_DESIGN.md sections 5 and 6, read against integrations/bloomberg/research/pull_consumer.py's process_one() and integrations/bloomberg/READ_HERE.md's sign-out rule; no single command decides it
acceptance.expect: a reading, recorded with no verdict
acceptance.output_evidence: SEAM_DESIGN.md section 5 states, and pull_consumer.py's process_one() implements: bloomberg_health() is called BEFORE every pull; on ok:False, packs/<security_key>/status.json is written {state: FAILED, reason: 'terminal signed out (bloomberg_health ok=False): <health error>'} and the SQS message is deleted -- no automatic retry, no sign-in attempt by this worker or this consumer. So an analyst who submits a ticker while the terminal is signed out would, once a consumer next drains the queue, see status.json move REQUESTED -> FAILED with a human-readable reason naming the health error -- a MARKED failure, not a page that looks like it is still fetching. The one honesty gap this design does NOT close: if NO consumer is running at all (the poller is a person-started/stopped process, or a daily-vehicle-invoked one-shot, per section 2 -- never a persistent service), a request sits at REQUESTED indefinitely with no FAILED/timeout state ever written, and status.json alone cannot distinguish 'about to be picked up' from 'no consumer will ever run.' SEAM_DESIGN.md section 6 states the measured latency (7.6s / 7.7s end to end for a cold request with the consumer launched in the same second) and is explicit that this number assumes a consumer is running; it does not assume an unbounded wait is honest UI behavior, but it also does not build a queue-age alarm (G-20 forbids one) or a status TIMEOUT state for an unattended queue -- left as a named gap for whichever cell next operationalizes the poller's own schedule.

acceptance.output_evidence: OFFICIAL-VS-IMPOSTOR TEST: stated as an OR of three checks -- (1) the company's own measured web presence links to the account by exact URL, (2) the platform's own verification mark is present, (3) the account's bio names the company's registered domain via the display_link-vs-link discipline. It clears the bar PART V asks for in the trivial case (a same-name fan/parody account with NO cross-link, NO verification mark and a bio naming nothing) -- that account satisfies none of the three ORs and is correctly excluded, which a bare name-match rule would not do. DECLARED WEAKEST LINK, read honestly: the composition is an OR across three checks of very different strength, and check (3) alone is CHEAPLY GAMEABLE -- an impostor account can copy the same 'official account of <domain>' bio text a real one would carry, and the test as written admits it on that basis alone, with no requirement that (3) co-occur with (1) or (2). Check (2) is also weaker than it reads today: on at least one major platform, a paid verification mark has been decoupled from identity verification since 2023, so 'the platform's own verification mark is present' is not the strong signal it would have been earlier -- the test does not name this caveat. Check (1) is the strong test (a link FROM a channel already trusted TO the account) but is currently UNUSABLE for all 89 names, because every ir_domain in AMGT-s-12's universe.json is itself UNRESOLVED at this cut (G-24) -- there is no 'company's own measured web presence' yet to link from. So, as stated, the schema is discriminating in principle against the CHEAP case (name alone) but not against a MODERATELY DETERMINED impostor who copies bio text, and its one strong check has nothing to run against yet. A tighter version would require (3) to co-occur with (1) or (2) rather than standing alone, and would flag (2) as weakened by the platform-verification change -- neither of which this schema states. PUBLISHER SEED RULE: an owner applying it needs only to find, in a landed battery finding, a domain named either as an Active estate Lambda's fetch target or as a `display_link` a proven IR-scan measurement resolved to -- both are checkable by reading the cited document section, without re-deriving the underlying research (the rule gives the exact two citations already, eb9cedded6 s.1 and s.3). The rule is honestly SELF-LIMITING rather than incomplete: the brief's own s.4 states the SERP scan 'not run at scale' over the other 88 names, so applying this rule today admits close to nothing beyond the two seeded domains until that scan runs -- a coverage limit the rule discloses (via its own citations) rather than a defect in its clarity. It also correctly excludes marketscreener.com by name, the one case this project has already measured as a trap, which shows the rule is not merely permissive.
